newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-ALL BLACKS EYE TRI-NATIONS TRIUMPH.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-ALL BLACKS EYE TRI-NATIONS TRIUMPH.

text.p: Holders New Zealand put one hand on the Tri-Nations championship with a 33-18 defeat of Australia on Saturday in front of a record 90,000-strong crowd at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.

One week after their thrilling victory over South Africa in the southern hemisphere series opener, the rampant All Blacks scored a three tries to two win dominating in all areas in the unfamiliar surroundings of the MCG, normally the home of Australian cricket and Aussie Rules football.
Once veteran centre Frank Bunce, scorer of two tries in the stirring comeback against the Springboks, crossed the line after 10 minutes, there was little doubt about the outcome.

Leading 30-6 mid-way through the second half, the tiring All Blacks, who complained bitterly beforehand about a lack of recovery time from their opening fixture, surrendered two late tries as Australia salvaged some respectability.
Winger Jeff Wilson and fullback Christian Cullen crossed the line either side of the half-time interval as the visitors stamped their obvious class on the match.
Fly-half Carlos Spencer converted all three tries and landed four penalties in a perfect kicking display.
Wallaby fullback Matt Burke replied with two first half penalties as the outclassed home side trailed 23-6 at the interval.
The match was already well beyond Australia's reach when scrumhalf George Gregan added a late converted try before centre Jason Little closed his side's losing margin with another try.
The attendance of 90,119 was a record for a test match on Australian soil.
The New Zealanders, cheered on by thousands of their compatriots who made the trip to Melbourne, thrived in the intense atmosphere.
With the return home fixtures against the Springboks and Australia to come, New Zealand appear poised to maintain their overwhelming domination of southern hemisphere rugby union.
The latest victory, their sixth successive win against Australia since 1994, was achieved on the strength of another inspirational display by captain Sean Fitzpatrick.
The veteran hooker was in doubt until only hours before kick-off because of a knee injury, but his mere presence appeared to stir his side.
Early on, his vast experience helped the All Blacks repeat the dominance in the forwards that paved the way for an easy 30-13 win against the Wallabies in Christchurch three weeks ago.
By winning in Melbourne, coach John Hart's side also lifted the Bledisloe Cup, the annual challenge between the two nations.
Australia's woes were compounded when fly-half Tim Horan left the field with a suspected broken thumb.

Australia - 15-Matt Burke, 14-Ben Tune, 13-Jason Little, 12-James Holbeck, 11-Joe Roff; 10-Tim Horan (Stephen Larkham, 40th), 9-George Gregan; 8-Michael Brial (Troy Coker, 36th), 7-Brett Robinson (David Wilson, 65th), 6-Daniel Manu, 5-John Eales (captain), 4-Garrick Morgan, 3-Andrew Heath, 2-Michael Foley, 1-Richard Harry.

New Zealand - 15-Christian Cullen, 14-Jeff Wilson (Adrian Cashmore, 41st), 13-Frank Bunce, 12-Alama Iremia, 11-Glen Osborne; 10-Carlos Spencer, 9-Justin Marshall; 8-Zinzan Brooke, 7-Josh Kronfeld, 6-Taine Randell, 5-Robin Brooke, 4-Ian Jones, 3-Olo Brown, 2-Sean Fitzpatrick (captain), 1-Craig Dowd.
